faq.a: People disagree because they have different life experiences, know different facts, care about different values, and have different feelings. Often both sides see part of the truth.
asks: Why do people have different opinions?

faq.q: How do life experiences shape opinions?
faq.a: Where we grow up, our family, culture and the things that have happened to us shape what we notice and what seems normal or important.
asks: Why do people from different places think differently?

faq.q: Can new facts end a disagreement?
faq.a: Sometimes. If people disagree because one knows something the other does not, sharing reliable facts can settle it. But when values differ, facts alone may not.
Values are the ideas we care about most, like fairness, kindness, freedom, safety, family or tradition. People rank them differently, which leads to different opinions.
Fear, anger or pride can make us cling to our view or stop listening. Calming down first helps people hear each other.

facts: Psychologist Jonathan Haidt's Moral Foundations research suggests people weigh values like care, fairness, loyalty and liberty differently.
The 6-or-9 picture is a popular way to show that two people can look at the same thing and honestly see it differently.

quiz.say: Two friends know the same facts about a new park but still disagree about it. What is the most likely reason?

options.show: One of them must be lying
options.say: One of them must be lying

quiz.why: People can weigh the same facts differently because they care about different things.

wrong.1: Honest people can disagree without lying.
wrong.2: Facts exist; people just weigh them differently.

options.show: People see things from different places
options.say: People see things from different places

wrong.0: Good people disagree all the time.
